title: New Zealand Recognizes a Mountain as a Legal Person
titleZh: 新西兰承认一座山为法律主体
credits: Charlotte Graham-McLay wrote this story for The Associated Press. Andrew Smith adapted it for VOA Learning English.

sentences.en: New Zealand’s parliament recently passed a law that gives a mountain all the rights and responsibilities of a human being.
sentences.zh: 新西兰议会最近通过了一项法律，赋予一座山与人类同等的所有权利和责任。

sentences.en: The indigenous Māori people of New Zealand consider the mountain their ancestor.
sentences.zh: 新西兰的土著毛利人将这座山视为他们的祖先。

sentences.en: The mountain is now known by its Māori name, Taranaki Maunga.
sentences.zh: 这座山现在以其毛利语名称塔拉纳基山（Taranaki Maunga）为人所知。

sentences.en: The Māori people of New Zealand represent about 15 percent of the country’s population.
sentences.zh: 新西兰的毛利人约占该国人口的15%。

sentences.en: Taranaki Maunga is a dormant volcano on New Zealand’s North Island.
sentences.zh: 塔拉纳基山是新西兰北岛上一座休眠火山。

sentences.en: Snow covers the top of the 2,516-meter-high mountain.
sentences.zh: 海拔2516米的山顶终年积雪。

sentences.en: It is a popular place for tourism, hiking and snow sports.
sentences.zh: 这里是旅游、徒步和滑雪的热门地点。

sentences.en: The legal recognition of the mountain is one of the steps New Zealand’s government has taken to make up for harm the indigenous population suffered in the past.
sentences.zh: 对这座山的法律承认是新西兰政府为弥补土著人口过去所受伤害而采取的举措之一。

sentences.en: The new law makes it known that the Taranaki area was stolen from the Māori after New Zealand was colonized.
sentences.zh: 新法律表明，在新西兰被殖民后，塔拉纳基地区的土地被从毛利人手中夺走。

sentences.en: The new law gives Taranaki Maunga all the rights, powers, duties, responsibilities and liabilities of a person.
sentences.zh: 新法律赋予塔拉纳基山作为一个人所享有的全部权利、权力、义务、责任和法律责任。

sentences.en: The law says a newly created group will be “the face and voice” of the mountain.
sentences.zh: 法律规定，一个新成立的团体将成为这座山的“面孔和声音”。

sentences.en: Four members from local Māori tribes and four members appointed by the country's conservation minister will be in the group.
sentences.zh: 该团体将由四名当地毛利部落成员和由该国保护部长任命的四名成员组成。

sentences.en: Paul Goldsmith is the lawmaker responsible for the legal settlements between the government and Māori tribes.
sentences.zh: 保罗·戈德史密斯是负责政府与毛利部落之间法律和解的立法者。

sentences.en: In a speech to Parliament, he said, “The mountain has long been an honored ancestor, a source of physical, cultural and spiritual sustenance and a final resting place."
sentences.zh: 他在议会上发表讲话说：“这座山长期以来一直备受尊崇，是身体、文化和精神滋养的源泉，也是最终的安息之地。”

sentences.en: Britain colonized New Zealand in the 1700s and 1800s.
sentences.zh: 英国在18世纪和19世纪殖民了新西兰。

sentences.en: In 1770, the British explorer Captain James Cook named the volcano Mount Egmont.
sentences.zh: 1770年，英国探险家詹姆斯·库克船长将这座火山命名为埃格蒙特山。

sentences.en: In 1840, Māori tribes and representatives of the British government signed the Treaty of Waitangi.
sentences.zh: 1840年，毛利部落与大英政府代表签署了《怀唐伊条约》。

sentences.en: The treaty promised the Māori would keep the rights to their land and resources.
sentences.zh: 该条约承诺毛利人将保留对其土地和资源的权利。

sentences.en: However, the British government began breaking parts of the treaty after that.
sentences.zh: 然而，此后英国政府开始违反条约的部分条款。

sentences.en: In 1865, the government took a large area of Taranaki land, including the mountain, to punish the Māori for rebelling against British rule.
sentences.zh: 1865年，政府夺取了塔拉纳基地区的大片土地，包括这座山，以惩罚毛利人对英国统治的反抗。

sentences.en: Over the next one hundred years, hunting and sports groups helped oversee how the land was used, but the Māori did not.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的百年间，狩猎和体育组织协助监管土地的使用方式，但毛利人却没有。

sentences.en: Goldsmith told the Associated Press that, in the past, Māori customs connected to the mountain were banned while the government supported tourism in the area.
sentences.zh: 戈德史密斯告诉美联社，在过去，与这座山相关的毛利习俗曾遭到禁止，而政府则支持该地区的旅游业。

sentences.en: The Māori protest movement of the 1970s and 1980s led to increased recognition of the Māori language, culture and rights in New Zealand’s law.
sentences.zh: 20世纪70年代和80年代的毛利人抗议运动，促进了新西兰法律对毛利语言、文化和权利的更多认可。

sentences.en: This has included billions of dollars to pay for the harm caused by breaking the Treaty of Waitangi.
sentences.zh: 这其中就包括数十亿美元，用于赔偿因违反《怀唐伊条约》所造成的伤害。

sentences.en: The mountain's legal rights are in place to support its health and wellbeing.
sentences.zh: 这座山的法定权利得以确立，以维护它的健康与福祉。

sentences.en: The law will support traditional uses of the land and calls for conservation work to protect the native wildlife.
sentences.zh: 该法律将支持对土地的传统使用，并呼吁开展保护本土野生动物的保护工作。

sentences.en: The mountain will remain open to the public.
sentences.zh: 这座山将继续向公众开放。

sentences.en: New Zealand was the first country in the world to recognize landforms as people.
sentences.zh: 新西兰是世界上第一个将地貌认定为“人”的国家。

sentences.en: In 2014, a law gave personhood to Te Urewera, a large forest on the North Island.
sentences.zh: 2014年，一部法律赋予了北岛一大片森林特雷乌拉（Te Urewera）以法人资格。

sentences.en: Government ownership ended and the Tūhoe tribe became its guardian.
sentences.zh: 政府所有权就此终结，图霍（Tūhoe）部落成为它的守护者。

sentences.en: And in 2017, New Zealand recognized the Whanganui River as a human, as part of a settlement with the tribe connected to the river.
sentences.zh: 2017年，新西兰将旺格努伊河（Whanganui River）承认为“人”，这是与与该河相关的部落达成和解的一部分。

sentences.en: All 123 lawmakers in Parliament supported the new law for Taranaki Maunga.
sentences.zh: 议会全部123名议员都支持关于塔拉纳基山（Taranaki Maunga）的新法律。

sentences.en: The unity of the vote was a change from recent disagreements in New Zealand about proposed changes to the Treaty of Waitangi itself.
sentences.zh: 投票的一致性与新西兰近期围绕对《怀唐伊条约》本身提出的修改所产生的分歧形成了转变。

sentences.en: In November, about 40,000 people marched to Parliament to protest a new law with proposed changes to the treaty.
sentences.zh: 11月，约4万人游行至议会，抗议一项拟对条约作出修改的新法律。

sentences.en: The protesters said the new law would take away Māori rights and harm the progress that has been made during the last 50 years.
sentences.zh: 抗议者称，这项新法律将会剥夺毛利人的权利，并损害过去50年间所取得的进展。

sentences.en: Most officials do not expect the bill with the proposed changes to become law.
sentences.zh: 大多数官员并不预计这项拟作修改的法律会成为法律。

sentences.en: I’m Andrew Smith.
sentences.zh: 我是安德鲁·史密斯。
